newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's disaster relief team ready for Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Canada's disaster relief team ready for Zaire.

text.p: Canadian teams specially trained for disaster relief are gathering at a military base in Ontario in preparation for their departure to Zaire, a Canadian military spokesman said on Thursday.

Members of Canada's Disaster Assistance Response Team (DART) are assembling at the base in Trenton, Ontario, about 100 miles (160 km) east of Toronto and a small reconnaisance force was expected to leave for Zaire on Thursday.
"If the green light comes on, they are already where the airlift is," Major Tony White, public affairs officer for the Canadian military, told Reuters.
The DART force could begin leaving Canada within days once the order is given.

"If this mission is mandated by the U.N. this afternoon and approved by the Canadian government thereafter, then there will be people heading to Zaire very shortly within a matter of days," said White.
The DART force for Zaire will comprise about 350 to 400 troops from various military units across Canada.
"People are drawn from units across the country to form a DART and that's what's going on right now," White said.
DART forces are a mix of medical, technical, engineering, communications and security experts plucked from various military units.
The DART forces were conceived by the Canadian military in 1994 after Canada sent a relief force to Rwanda to assist in the United Nations mission during the massacres there.

A DART force consists of 180 personnel able to deploy swiftly and conduct emergency relief operations for up to 40 days. The teams' goal typically is to bridge an emergency gap until a larger contingent from the international community can arrive to provide longer-term help.

A DART force has a tactical headquarters of about 35 people for command, communications and control. It also has an engineer troop of about 40, a medical platoon of about 45, an infantry platoon of about 35 and a logistics platoon of about 20 people.

In the case of an international mission, the DART can be activated either by a request from an individual country or by the United Nations. However, the final decision to deploy the force rests with the Canadian government.
